217	# Editing clips
218	
219	This page covers the edits you make to clips and to time on the timeline: putting clips on it, moving and trimming them, cutting, deleting and closing gaps, copying and pasting, and grouping clips into nests. Each edit is one undo step, and a gesture counts as one edit however long the drag lasts. When the project's rules won't allow an edit, the app beeps, changes nothing and tells you why.
220	
221	Changing a clip's speed, freezing a frame and reversing a clip are covered in [Speed](speed.md). Transitions are covered in [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md). Selecting, zooming, scrubbing and the track headers are covered in [Timeline](timeline.md).
222	
223	## What an edit acts on
224	
225	Most commands act on the **selection**, the clips outlined in coral on the timeline. Some also use the **playhead**, the **in/out range**, or the **current track**:
226	
227	- **The selection.** Click a clip to select it. ⇧-click adds a clip or takes it out. Drag from empty space to select by marquee. ⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select All**), ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**, every clip that starts at or after the playhead) and **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** also select. ⌥-clicking a track header selects every clip on that track. See [Timeline](timeline.md).
228	- **The playhead.** Split, trim to playhead, freeze frame, paste, insert and overwrite all work at the playhead.
229	- **The in/out range.** I sets the in point, O sets the out point and ⌥X clears both (**Mark ▸ Set In / Set Out / Clear Range**). With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range instead.
230	- **The current track** is the track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. Close Gap, Select All on Track, and Insert / Overwrite at Playhead use it.
231	
232	Clips on a **locked** track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled. A marquee skips them, and the edits that shift everything later in time leave them where they are. See [Limits](#limits).
233	
234	*Agents:* `set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the same view state. They are not edits and make no undo step.
235	
236	## Adding clips from the Media tab
237	
238	Drag a file's row from the Media tab onto a track. What the drop does depends on the modifier keys you hold **when you release**:
239	
240	| Drop | What it does | Undo name |
241	|---|---|---|
242	| No modifier | Places the whole file as a clip at the drop point. Nothing else moves. The drop is refused if the clip would overlap its neighbours in a way the overlap rule forbids. | Add Clip |
243	| ⌥ | **Insert.** Splits the clip under the drop point on that track, pushes everything on every unlocked track later by the file's length, then places the file in the gap. Only the destination track is cut. Clips on other tracks that span the drop point stay where they are, uncut; only clips that start at or after it move later. The exception is a detached sound linked to a clip that is cut: it is cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step. | Insert |
244	| ⇧⌥ | **Overwrite.** Clears the file's length from the drop point on that track alone, cutting at both ends and removing what lies between, then places the file. Nothing moves and no other track is touched, except that a detached sound linked to a clip that is cut is cut at the same points; its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked. | Overwrite |
245	
246	Dropping a row on the **preview canvas** adds the file at the playhead on a new track at the front.
247	
248	The same two placements also work without dragging. Select a row in the Media tab, then choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**. They place the file on the current track at the playhead. Neither has a shortcut. Right-clicking a row gives you the same two items for that file. Both are greyed out when no media row is selected, and for a `.cube` LUT, which is applied as a look rather than placed (see [Colour grading](color-grading.md)).
249	
250	A new clip covers the whole file, rounded down to whole frames so it never runs past the end of the file. Footage larger than the canvas is fitted when the project's fit-new-clips setting is on. Importing files is covered in [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md).
251	
252	*Agents:* `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` take `track`, `media` and `at`.
253	
254	## Moving clips
255	
256	Drag a clip's body to move it in time. Drag it up or down to move it to another track. If several clips are selected, dragging any one of them moves them all and keeps their timing and track offsets. Starts stop at zero.
257	
258	- **Onto a new track:** drop above the top lane to make a new front track, or below the bottom lane to make a new back track.
259	- **Duplicate while dragging:** hold ⌥ when you press. Copies are dragged and the originals stay put (undo name "Duplicate Clips").
260	- **Refused drops spring back.** If the drop breaks the overlap rule (see [Limits](#limits)), the clip animates back to where it was and nothing changes. While you drag, positions the project refuses are skipped, and the clip stays at the last allowed position.
261	- **Overlaps make transitions.** A clip dropped so it overlaps the clip before it on the same track gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Clips never push each other out of the way. Other edits do the same; see [Overlaps make transitions](#overlaps-make-transitions).
262	
263	The whole drag is one undo step, "Move Clips".
264	
265	### Nudging
266	
267	`,` and `.` move the selection one frame earlier or later. With ⇧ they move it ten frames. A nudge is an ordinary move, so the overlap rule can refuse it (undo name "Nudge Clips").
268	
269	*Agents:* `move_clip` takes `clips` and a `delta` in ticks. The optional `track` is the destination track for the first clip; the others keep their track offsets from it. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks.
270	
271	## Trimming
272	
273	Drag either edge of a clip to trim it. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip: the pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and the selected clip shows trim grips. A clip too narrow on screen (under about 21 points) has no edges, so zoom in to trim it. Clips on locked tracks show no resize cursor.
274	
275	- A **start trim** moves the clip's start and its in point together, so the frame under the edge stays put and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.
276	- An **end trim** moves the clip's end.
277	- A clip always keeps at least one frame. A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. Stills, text, shapes and graphics have no file length, so they trim freely.
278	- The whole drag is one undo step, "Trim Clip".
279	
280	To trim to the playhead, press **W** (**Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**) or **E** (**Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead**), or click the matching buttons in the timeline bar. They trim each selected clip that the playhead is inside. If the playhead isn't inside any selected clip, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. W undoes as "Trim Start" and E as "Trim End", one step for all the clips they trim.
281	
282	### Rate stretch
283	
284	Hold ⌥ while you drag a media clip's **end** edge to stretch it instead. The clip's speed changes so that the same content fills the new length (undo name "Rate Stretch"). ⌥ on the start edge does an ordinary trim. If a stretch would take the clip above the speed where its sound is dropped, the app asks first. Speeds and their limits are covered in [Speed](speed.md).
285	
286	*Agents:* `trim_start` and `trim_end` take `clip` and `to`. `rate_stretch` takes `clip` and `to_end`.
287	
288	## Slip and roll
289	
290	Both keep something fixed on purpose.
291	
292	| Gesture | What it does | Undo name |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| ⌥⇧-drag a clip's body | **Slip.** The clip stays where it is on the timeline, at the same length, and the footage slides underneath it. You choose which part of the file it shows. It stops when the clip reaches either end of the file. A still slips the frame it holds. | Slip |
295	| ⌥⇧-drag a clip's edge | **Roll.** Moves a cut between two clips that touch. One clip gets longer and the other gets shorter by the same amount, and nothing else moves. Each clip keeps at least one frame and can't extend past its own file. | Roll |
296	
297	A slip doesn't snap, because the timeline's snap points mean nothing inside the footage. It still moves in whole frames. A roll snaps like a trim.
298	
299	A roll needs two clips that touch exactly. The start edge rolls the cut with the clip before, and the end edge rolls the cut with the clip after. Where there is a gap or an overlap (a transition) at that edge, there is no cut to roll and the drag does nothing. A slip on a clip with nothing to slip, such as text, a shape or a nest, is an error.
300	
301	*Agents:* `slip` takes `clip` and `delta`. `roll` takes `clip` (the clip to the right of the cut) and `to`. A roll is refused with "no clip on track … ends where clip … begins" when the clips don't touch.
302	
303	## Splitting
304	
305	**Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T, or the scissors button in the timeline bar) cuts at the playhead:
306	
307	- With clips selected, it cuts each selected clip the playhead is strictly inside.
308	- With nothing selected, it cuts every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track.
309	
310	The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped. Animation actions stay with the piece they fall in, and an action that spans the cut becomes two. Caption word timings stay on their words.
311	
312	*Agents:* `split` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and optional `clips`. Without `clips` it cuts every unlocked clip at that time.
313	
314	### Split at Shot Changes
315	
316	**Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes** cuts each selected clip of a video file at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays: a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording comes apart into one clip per shot, as one undo step ("Split at Shot Changes"). It is on when a selected clip shows a video file's picture; any other clip in the selection is left alone.
317	
318	Frame Job finds the cuts on this Mac, with nothing sent anywhere and no key needed, and keeps them in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. While they are being found the **Analyzing** sheet shows each file with a bar: "Waiting" until its first frame is read, then the share done, then "Done". **Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing; what was already found stays in the cache. If you change the project while the sheet is up, nothing is split and the inspector says to choose the command again.
319	
320	- Each cut lands on the timeline's frame grid, through the clip's speed, ramp and reversal. A cut within one frame of either end of a clip is not made.
321	- A clip on a locked track is still cut, and its linked sound is cut with it when the sound is on an unlocked track, as **Split** does.
322	- If the splits would take the project past 4,096 clips, counting each linked clip they also cut, nothing is split and the inspector says how many clips it would add and how many fit.
323	- A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. A gradual dissolve is not a cut, and a single flash frame is not one. A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
324	
325	*Agents:* `split_at_shots` takes optional `clips`; without them it splits every clip of a video file on an unlocked track. It waits up to 60 s for the cuts to be found and shows no sheet, and it answers each clip's cuts and how many clips it added.
326	
327	## Deleting
328	
329	The two delete keys pair up. Each acts on the selection, or on the in/out range when nothing is selected. The difference is whether the hole closes.
330	
331	| Command | Selection | In/out range, nothing selected |
332	|---|---|---|
333	| **Edit ▸ Delete** (⌫) | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range and removes what lies between. Nothing moves, markers included. |
334	| **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** (⌘⌫, or the timeline bar's button) | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips, then closes each hole they leave. Everything later on every unlocked track moves left by the hole's length. | **Ripple Delete:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range, removes what lies between, and closes the hole. |
335	
336	- Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch. A clip past several holes moves by their combined length. Clips on other tracks that span the hole stay where they are. **Markers don't move** in a ripple delete.
337	- With an animation action selected, ⌫ removes that action instead of its clip. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).
338	- With words selected in the Transcript tab, ⌫ (and ⌘⌫) deletes those words and **closes** the gap, as deleting text does, while ⌫ on the timeline leaves one. See [The Transcript](transcript.md#cutting-by-deleting-words).
339	- Both items are greyed out while you are typing in a text field, so ⌫ and ⌘⌫ still edit text there. They are also greyed out when nothing is selected and no range is set.
340	- **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…** and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** each make many ripple cuts as a single undo step. See [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md).
341	
342	*Agents:* `delete` and `ripple_delete` take `clips`. `lift_range` and `ripple_delete_range` take `from` and `to`; a reversed pair means the same range. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes a list of `[from, to]` pairs. It merges pairs that touch or overlap, then cuts them all as one edit.
343	
344	## Closing gaps and inserting time
345	
346	**Double-click an empty stretch of a lane** to close that gap. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. **Clip ▸ Close Gap** does the same for the gap under the playhead on the current track. A gap before the first clip of a track closes back to zero. Undo name: "Close Gap".
347	
348	A gap closes completely or not at all. The edit is refused when:
349	
350	- the point you chose is on a clip, not in a gap;
351	- no clip follows the gap;
352	- the track is locked;
353	- closing it would push clips on another track into an overlap the overlap rule forbids.
354	
355	**Inserting time** opens empty room instead. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after it. Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut (split first if you want the room inside a clip). No menu item or gesture does this on its own. ⌥-drop insert and Freeze Frame both use it as part of their edit, and agents can call it directly.
356	
357	To open room by hand, press ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) and drag the selected clips later, or nudge them with ⇧. (period). Unlike Insert Time, this also moves selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are.
358	
359	*Agents:* `close_gap` takes `track` and `at`. `insert_time` takes `at` and `length`.
360	
361	## Duplicating
362	
363	**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (⌘D, or the timeline bar's button) puts a copy of each selected clip on the same track, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing. The duplicate is refused if the copies would break the overlap rule. To place copies somewhere else, ⌥-drag instead (see [Moving clips](#moving-clips)).
364	
365	*Agents:* `duplicate` takes `clips`.
366	
367	## Copy, cut and paste
368	
369	| Command | Shortcut | What it does |
370	|---|---|---|
371	| **Edit ▸ Copy** | ⌘C | Puts the selected clips on the clipboard, with the media files they show. A selected picture brings its detached sound along, so the pair pastes as a pair; a selected detached sound is copied on its own. Pasted into a text editor, they arrive as a one-line summary such as "Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00". |
372	| **Edit ▸ Cut** | ⌘X | Copies, then deletes the selection and leaves gaps, as ⌫ does. One undo step. |
373	| **Edit ▸ Paste** | ⌘V | Pastes the clipboard's clips at the playhead, then selects them. |
374	| **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** | ⌥⌘V | Copies the copied clip's look onto every selected clip. |
375	| **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties** | — | Copies a copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips drawn by the same graphic. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |
376	
377	Cut and Copy are greyed out with nothing selected. Paste is greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard; it never pastes another app's text or files. Paste Attributes also needs a selection, and Paste Graphic Properties a selected graphic clip.
378	
379	**Paste** keeps the copied arrangement. The earliest clip lands at the playhead and the others keep their distance from it. The copied front-most lane goes onto the front track, the lanes behind it onto the tracks behind, and tracks are added at the back if there aren't enough. A pasted clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new track at the front, so a paste is never refused for lack of room. You can paste into another project. Media is matched by file path and added to the project when it isn't there yet. Pasted clips get new identities and are snapped to the project's frame rate.
380	
381	**Paste Attributes** takes the look of the copied clip that starts earliest, then replaces each matching group on every selected clip with it. A group is only copied when both clips have it:
382	
383	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
384	|---|---|---|
385	| Video | Everything: position, scale, rotation, crop, opacity, effects, grade | — |
386	| Audio | Everything: volume, pan, fades, effects | — |
387	| Text | Font, size, colours, layout, animation | Its own words and their timings |
388	| Shape | Fill, stroke, gradient and the rest of the style | Its kind, size and end points |
389	
390	The target keeps its place, length, speed, animation actions, transition, name, label, and which halves (picture and sound) are switched on. If nothing would change, it beeps.
391	
392	*Agents:* `paste` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and a `payload` shaped like what Copy writes, `{"clips": […], "media": […]}`. A payload clip's `track` is its depth from the front, 0 being the front-most lane. The optional `track` argument is the track id where depth 0 lands (default: the front track); deeper lanes follow behind it, and tracks are added as needed. `paste_attributes` takes `clips`, the same `payload`, and optional `groups` and `skip_missing`.
393	
394	## Splitting picture from sound
395	
396	**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (⌥⌘D) switches off each selected clip's sound and adds an audio-only copy of it on the track below, at the same time, with the same footage and speed. If the clip is on the back track, a new track is added behind it. Undo name: "Detach Audio".
397	
398	The two clips stay linked: moving, splitting, rippling, nesting or copying either one takes the other, and trimming the sound's edge alone makes a J-cut or an L-cut ([Audio](audio.md#j-cuts-and-l-cuts)). **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (⇧⌥⌘D) merges each pair back into one clip. Undo name: "Attach Audio".
399	
400	Each clip that can't be detached is refused with a reason: "clip … has no audio to detach: it is not a media clip", "…: media … has no audio track", or "…: its audio is switched off".
401	
402	A clip's picture and sound can each be switched on or off. The app's only control for this is Detach Audio. Agents can set either half directly.
403	
404	*Agents:* `detach_audio` takes `clip`, and `attach_audio` takes either half's `clip`. `set_enabled` takes `clip` and `video` and/or `audio` (true or false). Leave one out to keep its value.
405	
406	## Nests
407	
408	A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on, the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.
409	
410	### Making and opening up a nest
411	
412	**Clip ▸ Nest** (⌘G) groups the selected clips:
413	
414	- The new nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used. It runs from the earliest start to the latest end and is selected afterwards.
415	- Inside the nest, the clips keep their properties, actions and transitions, their timing relative to each other, and their stacking order.
416	- The nest's own canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the project size later doesn't re-lay out what's inside. To change a nest's size, un-nest it (⇧⌘G), change the project size if you need to, and nest again (⌘G). Opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.
417

    /// Every overlap on `track`, in time order.
    ///
    /// Only ADJACENT clips (in start order) are considered, which is the
    /// timeline's model of a transition: it sits between two neighbours.
    /// The overlap rule guarantees nothing else can overlap anyway, and
    /// [`Project::check_overlap_rule`] is what detects a project where
    /// something does.
    pub fn overlaps_on_track(&self, track: u32) -> Vec<Overlap> {
        let clips = self.clips_on_track(track);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for pair in clips.windows(2) {
            if let (Some(earlier), Some(later)) = (pair.first(), pair.get(1)) {
                if let Some(overlap) = overlap_of(earlier, later) {
                    out.push(overlap);
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

---
title: "How edits work"
description: What an edit acts on, why clips never push each other, and the rules every timeline edit keeps.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every edit in Frame Job acts on something you've already pointed at, and every edit keeps the same few rules. Once you know them, you can tell what a command will touch and why one sometimes won't go through.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
  where="The timeline: the selection, the playhead and the range"
  tools={['set_selection', 'set_playhead', 'set_range']}
/>

## What an edit acts on

Most commands act on the selected clips. Some also use the playhead, the in and out range or the current track.

| What | What it is | What uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The selection** | The clips outlined in coral on the timeline. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/). | Most commands |
| **The playhead** | The moment you're looking at. | Split, trim to the playhead, Freeze Frame, Paste, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
| **The in and out range** | The stretch between the points set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>. <kbd>⌥X</kbd> clears both. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range |
| **The current track** | The track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, it's a track inside the nest. | Close Gap, Select All on Track, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |

A selected clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), shows a dashed outline. Most edits take it along, as long as its track isn't locked.

## Clips never push each other

A clip you drag never shoves its neighbours out of the way. A place that would need a neighbour to move isn't available, so the clip [stops short of it](/editing/move-clips/#when-a-drop-wont-go-where-you-let-go).

Only the edits that are there to move other clips do so: [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/), [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/), [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). They open or close time across every unlocked track. A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) stays where it is.

## The overlap rule

Two clips on one track may overlap a little, and that overlap is a [transition](/motion/transitions/). The rule has three parts:

- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
- Each overlap can be at most half the length of the shorter clip.
- An adjustment clip can't overlap another clip at all, because it can't take a transition. Fade it with opacity instead.

An edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it gives that clip a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition.

Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests won't break the rule. Paste and Un-nest put a clip that would break it on a new track at the front instead. A ripple delete always goes through, and a clip it slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.

## Times land on frames

Every time you give an edit, by dragging or typing, lands on a whole frame of the project's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/). It goes to the nearest frame, so you can't place a clip between two frames. A time before the start of the timeline stops at 0.

The exception is a fade length typed in the Audio tab, which keeps the value you typed. A fade dragged by its handle on the clip still lands on a frame.

## One frame minimum

[Trims](/editing/trimming/) and [rolls](/editing/slip-and-roll/) always leave a clip at least one frame long. The drag stops there, however far you pull.

## Project limits

| A project holds up to | |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | 4,096 |
| Tracks | 64 |
| Levels of nesting | 8 |
| Markers | 1,024 |
| Media files | 1,024 |

Clips and tracks inside nests count towards the same totals as the ones on the timeline. An edit that would pass a limit doesn't happen, and the project stays as it was. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## When an edit doesn't go through

Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and adds no undo step. When a rule stopped the edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. An edit that would change nothing beeps too, with no reason given.

A drag is quieter. It stays at the last position the project allows, with no beep. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).

## With an agent

`set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the selection, the playhead and the range. They aren't edits and they add no undo step. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Good to know

A move or a ripple shifts every clip by exactly the same amount, so clips stay in step. At a frame rate that doesn't divide evenly, such as 7 fps, a shifted start can sit off the frame grid by a sliver too small to see.

## Related

- [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

---
title: "Add clips to the timeline"
description: Drag a file from the Media tab onto a track or the canvas, and see where it lands and what stops a drop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Importing a file puts it in the Media tab, not on the timeline. To use it, drag its row onto a track or onto the preview canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Media tab ▸ drag a row onto a track', 'Media tab ▸ drag a row onto the preview canvas']}
  tools={['add_clip', 'add_track']}
/>

This page covers files. [Text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) have their own ways in.

## Drag media onto a track

Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track. The whole file lands as one clip at the pointer, on the nearest frame, and nothing else moves. The drop doesn't snap to the edges of other clips.

Hold a modifier as you let go to make room for the file or replace what's there. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#drop-with-a-modifier).

A drop that overlaps a neighbour a little still lands, as long as it keeps to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), and makes a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.

**Edit ▸ Undo** names this step Add Clip.

## Drop media on the canvas

Drop a row on the preview canvas to add the file at the playhead, on a new track at the front. Use this to lay a file over everything else without looking for a free stretch of track.

The new track and the clip are one undo step, Add Clip. Modifier keys do nothing here.

## What a new clip covers

A new clip starts at the head of the file and runs its whole length, at normal speed. The length rounds down to whole frames, so the clip never runs past the end of the file. That can leave a part of a frame at the tail unused.

- **A picture** is 5 seconds long. [Trim it](/editing/trimming/) to any length.
- **A file larger than the canvas** is scaled to fit, while **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). It's on by default. A smaller file keeps its size.
- **A video or sound file shorter than one frame** of the project can't be placed, and Frame Job says so.

## When a drop doesn't land

| What happened | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| The clip would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) | Frame Job beeps, adds nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> as you drop to make room instead. |
| You let go above or below the lanes | The drag springs back. Only a [clip already on the timeline](/editing/move-clips/#move-a-clip-to-a-new-track) makes a new track that way. |
| You let go in another project's window | The drag springs back. A row can only be placed in its own project. |

A new clip starts at the head of the file and runs its whole length, at normal speed. The length rounds down to whole frames, so the clip never runs past the end of the file. That can leave a part of a frame at the tail unused.

---
title: "Insert and overwrite"
description: Bring a file into a cut that's already timed, either by making room for it or by replacing what's there.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Insert and Overwrite bring a file into a cut that's already timed. Insert makes room for it and pushes everything later along. Overwrite replaces what's there and moves nothing.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead']}
  keys={['⌥-drop', '⇧⌥-drop']}
  where="Right-click a row in the Media tab"
  tools={['insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip']}
/>

## Place a file at the playhead

<Steps>

1. Click the file's row in the Media tab.

2. Move the playhead to where the file should start.

3. To choose the track, select a clip on it. With nothing selected, the file goes on the front track.

4. Choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**.

</Steps>

Neither item has a shortcut. You can also right-click a row and choose either item there, which acts on that row and selects it.

The file lands on the [current track](/editing/how-edits-work/#what-an-edit-acts-on). With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, that's a track inside the nest.

## Drop with a modifier

Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track, and hold a modifier as you let go. Only the keys held at that moment count.

| Hold | What the drop does |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing, or <kbd>⇧</kbd> alone | [Adds the clip](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) without moving anything |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> | Inserts at the drop point |
| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> | Overwrites at the drop point |

The modifiers only work on a track. A drop on the preview canvas always [adds the file on a new track](/editing/add-clips/#drop-media-on-the-canvas).

## Insert a file

Insert keeps everything you've already cut, and the timeline gets longer by the length of the file.

- If the point falls inside a clip on the destination track, that clip is split there.
- Every unlocked track opens by the file's length. Clips that start at or after the point move later, and so do markers.
- The file lands in the room this makes.

Only the destination track is cut. A clip on another track that spans the point stays whole and where it is, so a music bed plays on unbroken under the new file. The exception is a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) linked to the clip that was cut. It's cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step.

The whole edit is one undo step, Insert.

## Overwrite with a file

Overwrite keeps the timeline's length, and what was there is gone.

- The destination track is cut at both ends of the file's length.
- Whatever lies between the cuts is removed.
- The file lands in the space.

Nothing shifts and no other track is touched. The exception is again a detached sound linked to a clip that was cut. It's cut at the same points, and its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked.

The whole edit is one undo step, Overwrite.

## Good to know

- **Locked tracks.** Insert won't work on a locked destination track, because the track can't open up, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Insert elsewhere leaves locked tracks where they are, so their clips can fall out of step with the rest. Overwrite still clears a locked track, because you named that track and nothing has to move.
- **When the menu items are dimmed.** They need a selected row in the Media tab, and that row can't be a `.cube` LUT. A LUT is [applied as a look](/color/luts/), so its right-click items are dimmed too. A filter that hides the selected row clears the selection.
- **The length is the whole file.** Both edits place the file from its first frame to its last. Trim the clip afterwards, or the room you've made shrinks only when you [ripple](/editing/delete-clips/).

## Related

- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)

---
title: "Move clips"
description: Drag clips along the timeline and between tracks, alone or together, and see what stops a drop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Drag a clip to change when it plays or which track it sits on. What you see while you drag is the real edit, so the preview and the timeline show the result as you go.

<AtAGlance
  where="Timeline ▸ drag a clip's body"
  keys={['⌘Z']}
  tools={['move_clip', 'undo']}
/>

## Drag a clip

Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.

The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.

You can't start a drag on a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

To drag a copy and leave the original, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).

## Move several clips together

Select the clips, then drag any one of them. They all move, and they keep their timing and their track offsets from each other. If the earliest clip reaches the start of the timeline, it stops at 0 and the others keep their distance from it.

## Move a clip to a new track

Let go above the top lane to make a new track at the front, or below the bottom lane to make a new track at the back. The new track and the move are one undo step.

## Clips that come along

A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves in time by the same amount and keeps its own track. So you can drag a sound onto a track of its own and its picture stays put. A partner on a locked track doesn't move.

## Overlaps make a transition

If you drop a clip so that it overlaps the clip before it on the track, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. The overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).

## When a drop won't go where you let go

While you drag, the clip only goes where the project allows. Over a position that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), it waits at the last position that was allowed, and catches up when you reach one that is.

If you let go over a position that isn't allowed, the clip stays at that last allowed position, and a ghost of it slides there from where you let go. If it never reached an allowed position, it's back where it started and nothing has changed. There's no beep and no message.

## One undo step per drag

A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts. **Edit ▸ Undo** names it Move Clips. A click that doesn't move the clip adds no undo step.

## Good to know

- A locked clip that's part of a selection moves with the others if you start the drag on an unlocked clip.
- With 64 tracks in the project, there's no new track to make. A drop above or below the lanes moves the clips in time only.
- To shift clips by an exact number of frames, [nudge them](/editing/nudge-clips/).

## Related

- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
- [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/)
- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)

title: "Nudge clips"
description: Move the selected clips one or ten frames at a time from the keyboard.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nudge moves the selected clips by an exact number of frames, for the small corrections that are hard to make with a drag.

<AtAGlance keys={[',', '.', '⇧,', '⇧.']} tools="move_clip" />

## Nudge the selection

| Keys | Moves the selection |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>,</kbd> | One frame earlier |
| <kbd>.</kbd> | One frame later |
| <kbd>⇧,</kbd> | Ten frames earlier |
| <kbd>⇧.</kbd> | Ten frames later |

Each press is one undo step, Nudge Clips. These are bare keys, so they type into a text field while one has the focus. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

A nudge is an ordinary [move](/editing/move-clips/), with the same rules:

- It beeps with nothing selected.

- A linked partner on an unlocked track moves with its clip.

A nudge moves a selected clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), which a drag won't start on. It doesn't snap, and it never changes a clip's track.

---
title: "Trim clips"
description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
  keys={['W', 'E']}
  where={[
    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
  ]}
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

## Drag an edge

Drag either edge of a clip. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip. The pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and a selected clip shows trim grips.

- **A clip 21 points wide or less** on screen is all body, so [zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) to trim it.
- **Clips on locked tracks** have no edges to grab and show no resize cursor.
- **A fade handle or an action band** under the pointer takes the press before the edge does.

The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) when snapping is on, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> turns snapping off for that moment. The whole drag is one undo step, Trim Clip.

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press a media clip's end edge to [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) it instead, which changes its speed to fill the new length. <kbd>⌥</kbd> on the start edge is an ordinary trim. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on either edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).

## What each edge does

**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.

**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.

Neither trim moves other clips, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, the edge waits at the last position that was allowed.

## Trim to the playhead

Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.

Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.

When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.

## Type a time

Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.

A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).

## How far a trim goes

A clip always keeps at least one frame.

A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds.

Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) hides what's inside it rather than cutting it.

## What a trim keeps

- **Linked sound.** Trim a picture and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) follows, if the two edges matched and the sound's track isn't locked. Trim the sound half and it goes alone, which is how you make a [J-cut or an L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> work the same way.
- **Actions.** They keep their time from the clip's start, so they stay put relative to the new start. An action past a new end is kept, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
- **Caption words.** Timed words stay on their speech.
- **Speed ramps.** On a [ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after a new start can change. The start stops where the clip still fits its media.

## Trim a graphic

Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation. The graphic's **In** moves forward, and its outro keeps its timing.

A graphic has no file to run out of, so you can also drag its start back earlier. **In** stops at 0, and the clip keeps growing.

Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

## With an agent

`trim_start` and `trim_end` can trim either half of a linked pair on its own. On the timeline, only the sound half trims alone. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

## Good to know

<kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> and the **In** and **Out** fields still trim a clip on a locked track, if you've selected it by clicking.

## Related

- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/)

---
title: "Trim clips"
description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
  keys={['W', 'E']}
  where={[
    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
  ]}
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

## Drag an edge

Drag either edge of a clip. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip. The pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and a selected clip shows trim grips.

- **A clip 21 points wide or less** on screen is all body, so [zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) to trim it.
- **Clips on locked tracks** have no edges to grab and show no resize cursor.
- **A fade handle or an action band** under the pointer takes the press before the edge does.

The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) when snapping is on, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> turns snapping off for that moment. The whole drag is one undo step, Trim Clip.

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press a media clip's end edge to [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) it instead, which changes its speed to fill the new length. <kbd>⌥</kbd> on the start edge is an ordinary trim. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on either edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).

## What each edge does

**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.

**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.

Neither trim moves other clips, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, the edge waits at the last position that was allowed.

## Trim to the playhead

Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.

Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.

When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.

## Type a time

Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.

A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).

## How far a trim goes

A clip always keeps at least one frame.

A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds.

Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) hides what's inside it rather than cutting it.

Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

---
title: "How edits work"
description: What an edit acts on, why clips never push each other, and the rules every timeline edit keeps.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every edit in Frame Job acts on something you've already pointed at, and every edit keeps the same few rules. Once you know them, you can tell what a command will touch and why one sometimes won't go through.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
  where="The timeline: the selection, the playhead and the range"
  tools={['set_selection', 'set_playhead', 'set_range']}
/>

## What an edit acts on

Most commands act on the selected clips. Some also use the playhead, the in and out range or the current track.

| What | What it is | What uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The selection** | The clips outlined in coral on the timeline. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/). | Most commands |
| **The playhead** | The moment you're looking at. | Split, trim to the playhead, Freeze Frame, Paste, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
| **The in and out range** | The stretch between the points set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>. <kbd>⌥X</kbd> clears both. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range |
| **The current track** | The track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, it's a track inside the nest. | Close Gap, Select All on Track, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |

A selected clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), shows a dashed outline. Most edits take it along, as long as its track isn't locked.

## Clips never push each other

A clip you drag never shoves its neighbours out of the way. A place that would need a neighbour to move isn't available, so the clip [stops short of it](/editing/move-clips/#when-a-drop-wont-go-where-you-let-go).

Only the edits that are there to move other clips do so: [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/), [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/), [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). They open or close time across every unlocked track. A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) stays where it is.

## The overlap rule

Two clips on one track may overlap a little, and that overlap is a [transition](/motion/transitions/). The rule has three parts:

- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
- Each overlap can be at most half the length of the shorter clip.
- An adjustment clip can't overlap another clip at all, because it can't take a transition. Fade it with opacity instead.

An edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it gives that clip a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition.

Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests won't break the rule. Paste and Un-nest put a clip that would break it on a new track at the front instead. A ripple delete always goes through, and a clip it slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.

## Times land on frames

Every time you give an edit, by dragging or typing, lands on a whole frame of the project's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/). It goes to the nearest frame, so you can't place a clip between two frames. A time before the start of the timeline stops at 0.

The exception is a fade length typed in the Audio tab, which keeps the value you typed. A fade dragged by its handle on the clip still lands on a frame.

## One frame minimum

[Trims](/editing/trimming/) and [rolls](/editing/slip-and-roll/) always leave a clip at least one frame long. The drag stops there, however far you pull.

## Project limits

| A project holds up to | |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | 4,096 |
| Tracks | 64 |
| Levels of nesting | 8 |
| Markers | 1,024 |
| Media files | 1,024 |

Clips and tracks inside nests count towards the same totals as the ones on the timeline. An edit that would pass a limit doesn't happen, and the project stays as it was. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## When an edit doesn't go through

Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and adds no undo step. When a rule stopped the edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. An edit that would change nothing beeps too, with no reason given.

A drag is quieter. It stays at the last position the project allows, with no beep. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).

## With an agent

`set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the selection, the playhead and the range. They aren't edits and they add no undo step. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Good to know

A move or a ripple shifts every clip by exactly the same amount, so clips stay in step. At a frame rate that doesn't divide evenly, such as 7 fps, a shifted start can sit off the frame grid by a sliver too small to see.

## Related

- [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

---
title: "Add clips to the timeline"
description: Drag a file from the Media tab onto a track or the canvas, and see where it lands and what stops a drop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Importing a file puts it in the Media tab, not on the timeline. To use it, drag its row onto a track or onto the preview canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Media tab ▸ drag a row onto a track', 'Media tab ▸ drag a row onto the preview canvas']}
  tools={['add_clip', 'add_track']}
/>

This page covers files. [Text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) have their own ways in.

## Drag media onto a track

Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track. The whole file lands as one clip at the pointer, on the nearest frame, and nothing else moves. The drop doesn't snap to the edges of other clips.

Hold a modifier as you let go to make room for the file or replace what's there. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#drop-with-a-modifier).

A drop that overlaps a neighbour a little still lands, as long as it keeps to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), and makes a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.

**Edit ▸ Undo** names this step Add Clip.

## Drop media on the canvas

Drop a row on the preview canvas to add the file at the playhead, on a new track at the front. Use this to lay a file over everything else without looking for a free stretch of track.

The new track and the clip are one undo step, Add Clip. Modifier keys do nothing here.

## What a new clip covers

A new clip starts at the head of the file and runs its whole length, at normal speed. The length rounds down to whole frames, so the clip never runs past the end of the file. That can leave a part of a frame at the tail unused.

- **A picture** is 5 seconds long. [Trim it](/editing/trimming/) to any length.
- **A file larger than the canvas** is scaled to fit, while **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). It's on by default. A smaller file keeps its size.
- **A video or sound file shorter than one frame** of the project can't be placed, and Frame Job says so.

## When a drop doesn't land

| What happened | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| The clip would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) | Frame Job beeps, adds nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> as you drop to make room instead. |
| You let go above or below the lanes | The drag springs back. Only a [clip already on the timeline](/editing/move-clips/#move-a-clip-to-a-new-track) makes a new track that way. |
| You let go in another project's window | The drag springs back. A row can only be placed in its own project. |

A `.cube` LUT row doesn't drag at all. [Apply it as a look](/color/luts/) instead.

## Good to know

- A plain drop onto a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) still places the clip, because nothing has to move.
- If the project already has 64 tracks, a drop on the canvas adds the file to the front track instead, and the overlap rule can stop it there.
- Files dragged from the Finder are different. On the Media tab they [import](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, each opens as a project of its own.

## Related

- [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/)
- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)

---
title: "Insert and overwrite"
description: Bring a file into a cut that's already timed, either by making room for it or by replacing what's there.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Insert and Overwrite bring a file into a cut that's already timed. Insert makes room for it and pushes everything later along. Overwrite replaces what's there and moves nothing.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead']}
  keys={['⌥-drop', '⇧⌥-drop']}
  where="Right-click a row in the Media tab"
  tools={['insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip']}
/>

## Place a file at the playhead

<Steps>

1. Click the file's row in the Media tab.

2. Move the playhead to where the file should start.

3. To choose the track, select a clip on it. With nothing selected, the file goes on the front track.

4. Choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**.

</Steps>

Neither item has a shortcut. You can also right-click a row and choose either item there, which acts on that row and selects it.

The file lands on the [current track](/editing/how-edits-work/#what-an-edit-acts-on). With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, that's a track inside the nest.

## Drop with a modifier

Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track, and hold a modifier as you let go. Only the keys held at that moment count.

| Hold | What the drop does |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing, or <kbd>⇧</kbd> alone | [Adds the clip](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) without moving anything |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> | Inserts at the drop point |
| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> | Overwrites at the drop point |

The modifiers only work on a track. A drop on the preview canvas always [adds the file on a new track](/editing/add-clips/#drop-media-on-the-canvas).

## Insert a file

Insert keeps everything you've already cut, and the timeline gets longer by the length of the file.

- If the point falls inside a clip on the destination track, that clip is split there.
- Every unlocked track opens by the file's length. Clips that start at or after the point move later, and so do markers.
- The file lands in the room this makes.

Only the destination track is cut. A clip on another track that spans the point stays whole and where it is, so a music bed plays on unbroken under the new file. The exception is a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) linked to the clip that was cut. It's cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step.

The whole edit is one undo step, Insert.

## Overwrite with a file

Overwrite keeps the timeline's length, and what was there is gone.

- The destination track is cut at both ends of the file's length.
- Whatever lies between the cuts is removed.
- The file lands in the space.

Nothing shifts and no other track is touched. The exception is again a detached sound linked to a clip that was cut. It's cut at the same points, and its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked.

The whole edit is one undo step, Overwrite.

## Good to know

- **Locked tracks.** Insert won't work on a locked destination track, because the track can't open up, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Insert elsewhere leaves locked tracks where they are, so their clips can fall out of step with the rest. Overwrite still clears a locked track, because you named that track and nothing has to move.
- **When the menu items are dimmed.** They need a selected row in the Media tab, and that row can't be a `.cube` LUT. A LUT is [applied as a look](/color/luts/), so its right-click items are dimmed too. A filter that hides the selected row clears the selection.
- **The length is the whole file.** Both edits place the file from its first frame to its last. Trim the clip afterwards, or the room you've made shrinks only when you [ripple](/editing/delete-clips/).

## Related

- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)

---
title: "Move clips"
description: Drag clips along the timeline and between tracks, alone or together, and see what stops a drop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Drag a clip to change when it plays or which track it sits on. What you see while you drag is the real edit, so the preview and the timeline show the result as you go.

<AtAGlance
  where="Timeline ▸ drag a clip's body"
  keys={['⌘Z']}
  tools={['move_clip', 'undo']}
/>

## Drag a clip

Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.

The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.

You can't start a drag on a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

To drag a copy and leave the original, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).

## Move several clips together

Select the clips, then drag any one of them. They all move, and they keep their timing and their track offsets from each other. If the earliest clip reaches the start of the timeline, it stops at 0 and the others keep their distance from it.

## Move a clip to a new track

Let go above the top lane to make a new track at the front, or below the bottom lane to make a new track at the back. The new track and the move are one undo step.

## Clips that come along

A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves in time by the same amount and keeps its own track. So you can drag a sound onto a track of its own and its picture stays put. A partner on a locked track doesn't move.

## Overlaps make a transition

If you drop a clip so that it overlaps the clip before it on the track, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. The overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).

## When a drop won't go where you let go

While you drag, the clip only goes where the project allows. Over a position that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), it waits at the last position that was allowed, and catches up when you reach one that is.

If you let go over a position that isn't allowed, the clip stays at that last allowed position, and a ghost of it slides there from where you let go. If it never reached an allowed position, it's back where it started and nothing has changed. There's no beep and no message.

## One undo step per drag

A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts. **Edit ▸ Undo** names it Move Clips. A click that doesn't move the clip adds no undo step.

## Good to know

- A locked clip that's part of a selection moves with the others if you start the drag on an unlocked clip.
- With 64 tracks in the project, there's no new track to make. A drop above or below the lanes moves the clips in time only.
- To shift clips by an exact number of frames, [nudge them](/editing/nudge-clips/).

## Related

- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
- [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/)
- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)

---
title: "Nudge clips"
description: Move the selected clips one or ten frames at a time from the keyboard.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nudge moves the selected clips by an exact number of frames, for the small corrections that are hard to make with a drag.

<AtAGlance keys={[',', '.', '⇧,', '⇧.']} tools="move_clip" />

## Nudge the selection

| Keys | Moves the selection |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>,</kbd> | One frame earlier |
| <kbd>.</kbd> | One frame later |
| <kbd>⇧,</kbd> | Ten frames earlier |
| <kbd>⇧.</kbd> | Ten frames later |

Each press is one undo step, Nudge Clips. These are bare keys, so they type into a text field while one has the focus. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

## Good to know

A nudge is an ordinary [move](/editing/move-clips/), with the same rules:

- It beeps with nothing selected.
- A nudge that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) beeps and changes nothing, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. A nudge that lands on a small enough overlap makes a Cross Dissolve.
- The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, so <kbd>⇧,</kbd> on a clip three frames from the start moves it three frames. A clip already at the start beeps.
- A linked partner on an unlocked track moves with its clip.

A nudge moves a selected clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), which a drag won't start on. It doesn't snap, and it never changes a clip's track.

## Related

- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

---
title: "Trim clips"
description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
  keys={['W', 'E']}
  where={[
    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
  ]}
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.

**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.

Neither trim moves other clips, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, the edge waits at the last position that was allowed.

## Trim to the playhead

Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.

Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.

When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.

## Type a time

Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.

A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).

## How far a trim goes

A clip always keeps at least one frame.

A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds.

Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) hides what's inside it rather than cutting it.

## What a trim keeps

- **Linked sound.** Trim a picture and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) follows, if the two edges matched and the sound's track isn't locked. Trim the sound half and it goes alone, which is how you make a [J-cut or an L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> work the same way.
- **Actions.** They keep their time from the clip's start, so they stay put relative to the new start. An action past a new end is kept, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
- **Caption words.** Timed words stay on their speech.
- **Speed ramps.** On a [ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after a new start can change. The start stops where the clip still fits its media.

## Trim a graphic

Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation. The graphic's **In** moves forward, and its outro keeps its timing.

A graphic has no file to run out of, so you can also drag its start back earlier. **In** stops at 0, and the clip keeps growing.

Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

## With an agent

`trim_start` and `trim_end` can trim either half of a linked pair on its own. On the timeline, only the sound half trims alone. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

## Good to know

<kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> and the **In** and **Out** fields still trim a clip on a locked track, if you've selected it by clicking.

13	/>
14	
15	## Drag a clip
16	
17	Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.
18	
19	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.

42	## When a drop won't go where you let go
43	
44	While you drag, the clip only goes where the project allows. Over a position that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), it waits at the last position that was allowed, and catches up when you reach one that is.
45	
46	If you let go over a position that isn't allowed, the clip stays at that last allowed position, and a ghost of it slides there from where you let go. If it never reached an allowed position, it's back where it started and nothing has changed. There's no beep and no message.
47	
48	## One undo step per drag
49	
50	A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts. **Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) names it Move Clips. A click that doesn't move the clip adds no undo step.
51	
52	## Good to know
53	
54	- A locked clip that's part of a selection moves with the others if you start the drag on an unlocked clip.
55	- With 64 tracks in the project, there's no new track to make. A drop above or below the lanes moves the clips in time only.
56	- To shift clips by an exact number of frames, [nudge them](/editing/nudge-clips/).

58	## Related
